original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Independent hypothesis-by-hypothesis review of the PR3259 fixed-cover support-cut embedding argument (and PR3252's memory-relaxation proof, and what PR3427 consumes). PR3427's one-recombined-helper criterion (which PR3427 already calls exact for the pooled untimed relaxation) is re-proved and evaluated on all 104 columns, with its closed form, vertex cover and rank consequences, single-relaxation support rows and a small-domain exhaustive check. Audit only; author-checked and AI-assisted.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a chronological correction program. The revision-6 decisions table (row 1) instead asks first for a review of the submitted #3259 support cut and its contract, which decides whether the fixed-cover route is closed and what any reopening must cover. No construction is attempted.
bottleneck_link: Decides whether the pooled fixed-cover, frozen-path, immutable-X, unread-Y, independent-dirt, monotone equal-frame P104 contract is closed and how large its obstruction is (2,682 unsupported required entries, not one), which bounds what a contract change or source preconditioner must reopen before any construction round.
stop_rule: Stop at a proof-review verdict per step; on an engine disagreement, a proof gap or an oracle escape, stop and minimize. No matching search, no correction construction, no pricing beyond counting witness operations, at most three new relaxation rows, no Lean. Deviation: five rows were delivered, relaxing three hypotheses (K5 as R1, R1c and R1u, the last added at a round-1 review's request; K1 as R2; K6 as R3).
evidence: PROOF-REVIEW.md (step table a-h, lemma proof, PR3252 review, PR3427 consumption, rank consequence, load-bearing rows); verify.py (exact channel run of 4,058 events: Y increment = G/2; layered control reproducing PR3259 numbers; sharp support by one criterion in two loop orders and by an independent PR3252 full-memory recurrence over all 104 columns (PR3427 ran the same operations on its four columns), all equal, shape = 2,309 own port pairs + (73,83), with routes asserted (31 own pairs also admitted by another type; (73,83) only by type (17,147), X83's dim-4 frame to Y73's cap); PR3427 four-column masks, which exclude 92 required entries that PR3259's test grants; perfect matching of the 2,682 missing entries (vertex cover 104); rank(U-I)>=23 from a maximum independent 23x23 principal block, size checked by two exact searches, rank by Fraction elimination, det(2C[S,S])=2^30 by Bareiss; rank(G/2)=8, so any unsupported rectangle has rank at most 31; rows R1/R1u/R1c/R2/R3; 9,000 seeded small instances with exhaustive untimed reachability, 13,242 realized checked programs and 18,000 random legal programs (9,000 directed, run in the checked interpreter; 9,000 uniform, legal by construction), exact Fractions; six in-verifier contract-violation controls); test_verify.py (seven tests: four defect controls with their own FAIL messages and three fact checks, including a containment-free variant that grants an unreachable pair).

open_questions.question: What rank does the full unsupported pattern force on a P104 source preconditioner (U-I)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A maximum unsupported principal block already gives rank(U-I)>=23 versus PR3427's 4, and no principal block does better; a non-principal rectangle or a min-rank completion of -C on all 8,506 unsupported pairs may force more and would further constrain joint native source preparation. Any unsupported rectangle C[R,S] has rank at most |R & S| + 8 <= 31, since the common ports R & S are independent and rank(G/2) = 8 (asserted).
open_questions.first_step: Search non-principal rectangles up to the cap of 31, or bound the min-rank completion exactly, with the pinned sharp support; no matching search.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing beyond the sharp support certificate here; pricing a joint preparation remains separate.

open_questions.question: Which changed contract supports all 4,992 required entries, in particular the 2,682 sharp-missing ones, at least cost, and what is its full bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Under the present cover the supported entries are exactly those whose own slot pair is compatible, plus (73,83); relaxing the cover (R2) reopens every entry at support level, but its cost is unknown. The missing entries need a vertex cover of 104, so path changes alone must touch at least 104 registers. Pending #3618's T48 (one target lift, +2 rank mass, a whole row) changes the target path instead and is the first priced data point; additivity across rows is not established.
open_questions.first_step: Name the changed hypothesis among K1-K7 (or added storage), support all 4,992 required entries at support level (a changed cover or path can lose some of the 2,310 pairs supported now), and list each added operation.
open_questions.blocked_by: Coefficients, dirty restoration, chronology, native/hosting/precision/consumer costs are unknown.

open_questions.question: Is there a coefficient-level correction that reads channel state (R1c/R3) and restores it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Channel state already carries the support of G/2, so support tests reopen everything; only a coefficient-level construction can decide this route.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one target row, the channel registers read, the restoration of each, and the changed channel obligations.
open_questions.blocked_by: Changed original channel; restoration and pricing unknown.
